blocks.title: Honors — interrogate what you built
blocks.markdown: Yesterday you derived $F = ma$ and defined the newton. A model you can't attack you don't really trust. Today you go after your own equation: where does the experiment lie, and what does the equation quietly assume?

blocks.title: Your 'constant force' wasn't constant
blocks.markdown:
The force in the vary-force lab came from a **hanging mass** pulling the cart. But here's the flaw: that hanging mass is *accelerating downward too* — it's part of the moving system, so the tension pulling your cart is **less than** the hanging weight, and it isn't truly fixed as you change the cart's load.

So the 'constant force' label on your data is an approximation, not a fact. Think about which way that flaw would bend your $a$-vs-$F$ line — and why CPA can use the data anyway while honors has to name the error.

## Where else does the equation strain?

Two more cracks worth seeing before you walk away trusting $F = ma$:

- **Friction and the track** ate some of your force, so the *net* force on the cart was a little less than what you applied — a systematic offset, not random scatter.
- **$F = ma$ assumes the mass is fixed.** It's silent about what happens if the moving thing *throws mass off* while it accelerates. Nothing in your derivation covers that case — the law simply doesn't apply when $m$ changes mid-motion.

blocks.frame: F = ma assumes the mass stays fixed. A real asteroid deflection works by ___, which throws mass off — so F = ma alone can't handle it. The later unit that does is ___, because ___.
blocks.prompt: TRANSFER (homework): $F = ma$ assumes a fixed mass. But a real deflection mission moves an asteroid by *throwing mass off* it — ejecting material so the rest recoils. That breaks the fixed-mass assumption you found today. Name the later unit that has to handle changing-mass problems, and explain why $F = ma$ by itself can't.

blocks.title: Close forward
blocks.markdown: You now own the most important equation of the year — *and* you've located the two assumptions hiding inside it: fixed mass, and a clean isolated force. Units 3 and 4 exist to attack exactly those two assumptions. You already know where they'll strike.
